ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An ant walked $6 \mathrm{~m}$ every day to go from point $A$ to point $B$ in a straight line. One day Johnny put a straight cylinder of one meter high in that way. Now the ant walks on the same straight line or above it, having to go up and down the cylinder, as shown in the picture. How much does she have to walk now to go from $A$ to $B$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The red line segment in the figure represents the original straight-line path from A to B, and this straight line passes through the base area of a vertical cylinder. The cylinder blocks the road, and the figure also uses dashed lines to indicate that the ant's path still follows the direction of this straight line or is directly above it: it needs to climb vertically to the top surface of the cylinder, pass above, and then come down vertically to return to the original straight-line path. Reasoning: The original straight-line distance from A to B is 6 m. The projection of the new route in the horizontal direction is still just the original straight line from A to B, so the total length of all horizontal or top-passing parts is still 6 m. The cylinder is 1 m high, and the ant has to climb up an additional 1 m and then climb down 1 m. Therefore the total distance is 6 + 1 + 1 = 8 m.
